PayGuard version 15 scores better offline than version 14. Should it replace v14 for every payment right now? Not yet. Offline tests use old data; real traffic can still surprise you. A safe update answers three questions: **exactly what changed, how do we expose it gradually, and how do we undo it in one step?**

::: {.callout-tip}
## What you will learn
- The six things you must version together
- Semantic versions and registry aliases such as "champion" and "challenger"
- Shadow, canary, blue-green and A/B releases, and when to use each
- An animated canary release that rolls itself back when things go wrong
:::

{{< include ../_series-nav.md >}}

## Version everything that changes the prediction

A model's output depends on more than the model file. If any of these change silently, you cannot reproduce or explain a prediction.

| Artifact | Example | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| Code | Feature functions, training script | Git commit |
| Data | Training snapshot of 2026-09-01 | DVC, lakeFS, dated tables |
| Features | Definition of `tx_last_hour` | Feature store, code review |
| Model | `payguard` version 15 | MLflow Model Registry |
| Config | Threshold 0.5, hyperparameters | Config file in Git |
| Environment | Python 3.11, scikit-learn 1.5 | Docker image tag |

: What to version {#tbl-version}

A simple semantic scheme makes versions readable:

- **MAJOR** (2.0.0): the input or output contract changes, for example a new required field. Callers must update.
- **MINOR** (1.5.0): retrained on new data or with new internal features, same contract.
- **PATCH** (1.5.1): a bug fix that does not change model behaviour intentionally.

Over time, model versions branch and merge like code:

```{mermaid}
%%| echo: false
gitGraph
  commit id: "v1.0 first model"
  commit id: "v1.1 monthly retrain"
  branch experiment
  commit id: "new feature: merchant age"
  commit id: "tuned depth"
  checkout main
  commit id: "v1.2 monthly retrain"
  merge experiment id: "v1.3 adds merchant age"
  commit id: "v2.0 new input schema"
```

## The model registry

A **registry** stores every model version with its metrics and lineage. Instead of hard-coding "version 15", the service loads a model by **alias**. Promoting or rolling back means moving the alias, with no code change and no redeploy ([MLflow docs](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/ml/model-registry/)).

```{.python filename="promote.py"}
import mlflow
from mlflow import MlflowClient

client = MlflowClient()
# v15 passed the quality gate: make it the challenger
client.set_registered_model_alias("payguard", "challenger", 15)

# the service always loads whatever "champion" points to
model = mlflow.pyfunc.load_model("models:/payguard@champion")

# after a successful rollout, promote; rolling back is the same call with 14
client.set_registered_model_alias("payguard", "champion", 15)
```

## Four ways to roll out

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import {ms, msStyle} from "/assets/js/ms-plot.js"
viewof strat = Inputs.radio(["Shadow", "Canary", "Blue-green", "A/B test"], {value: "Canary", label: "Strategy"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const info = {
    "Shadow": {split: [100, 0], note: "v15 receives a copy of every request, but its answers are only logged. Zero user risk; compare predictions side by side.", dashed: true},
    "Canary": {split: [95, 5], note: "A small slice of real traffic goes to v15. If its metrics hold, the slice grows step by step.", dashed: false},
    "Blue-green": {split: [0, 100], note: "v15 runs on a full copy of the environment. Traffic switches all at once, and switching back is instant.", dashed: false},
    "A/B test": {split: [50, 50], note: "Traffic is split randomly for a fixed period to measure the business effect with statistics.", dashed: false}
  }[strat];
  const W = 760, H = 210;
  const y1 = 55, y2 = 155, wA = 2 + info.split[0] / 8, wB = info.dashed ? 4 : 2 + info.split[1] / 8;
  return htl.html`<div>${htl.svg`<svg viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H}" style="width:100%;max-width:${W}px;font-family:Inter,system-ui,sans-serif">
    <rect x="20" y="80" width="130" height="50" rx="12" fill="${ms.slate}" fill-opacity="0.85"/>
    <text x="85" y="110" text-anchor="middle" fill="white" font-size="14" font-weight="600">Traffic</text>
    <path d="M150,105 C300,105 330,${y1} 520,${y1}" fill="none" stroke="${ms.indigo}" stroke-width="${wA}" stroke-opacity="0.8"/>
    <path d="M150,105 C300,105 330,${y2} 520,${y2}" fill="none" stroke="${ms.teal}" stroke-width="${wB}" stroke-opacity="0.8" stroke-dasharray="${info.dashed ? "6,5" : "none"}"/>
    <rect x="520" y="${y1 - 25}" width="210" height="50" rx="12" fill="${ms.indigo}" fill-opacity="0.85"/>
    <text x="625" y="${y1 + 5}" text-anchor="middle" fill="white" font-size="14" font-weight="600">v14 champion · ${info.split[0]}%</text>
    <rect x="520" y="${y2 - 25}" width="210" height="50" rx="12" fill="${ms.teal}" fill-opacity="0.85"/>
    <text x="625" y="${y2 + 5}" text-anchor="middle" fill="white" font-size="14" font-weight="600">v15 · ${info.dashed ? "copy only" : info.split[1] + "%"}</text>
  </svg>`}<div class="ms-readout"><span>${strat}</span><b style="font-size:1rem">${info.note}</b></div></div>`;
}
```

| Strategy | User risk | Extra cost | Answers the question |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shadow | None | Double compute | Does it behave sanely on real inputs? |
| Canary | Small, limited to the slice | Low | Is it safe to roll out? |
| Blue-green | Brief, but instant rollback | Two environments | Can we switch cleanly? |
| A/B test | Half of users see the new model | Time | Is it better for the business? |

: Rollout strategies {#tbl-rollout}

A common sequence for PayGuard is **shadow for a few days, then canary, then full rollout**, with an A/B test when the change affects business outcomes such as false declines.

## An animated canary release

Press play. Traffic to v15 steps up through 1%, 5%, 25%, 50% and 100%. At every step the system compares v15's error rate with v14's. Tick "bad release" to see the automatic rollback.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof badRelease = Inputs.toggle({label: "Bad release (v15 has a bug)", value: false})
viewof tol = Inputs.range([0.2, 2], {value: 0.5, step: 0.1, label: "Rollback if v15 errors exceed v14 by (percentage points)"})
viewof go_ = Inputs.button("Play rollout")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
canary = {
  const steps = [1, 5, 25, 50, 100], per = 30, rnd = d3.randomNormal.source(d3.randomLcg(13))(0, 0.12);
  const out = []; let rolled = -1;
  for (let t = 0; t < steps.length * per; t++) {
    const share = rolled >= 0 ? 0 : steps[Math.floor(t / per)];
    const base = 0.8 + rnd();
    const v15 = badRelease ? 0.8 + 1.6 * Math.min(1, t / 40) + rnd() * 1.5 : 0.75 + rnd() * (share < 5 ? 2.5 : 1);
    out.push({t, share, base, v15: rolled >= 0 ? null : v15});
    if (rolled < 0 && t % per === per - 1 && d3.mean(out.slice(-per), d => d.v15) - d3.mean(out.slice(-per), d => d.base) > tol) rolled = t;
  }
  return {out, rolled};
}
frame = {
  go_; canary;
  for (let i = 1; i <= canary.out.length; i++) { yield i; await Promises.delay(35); }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const shown = canary.out.slice(0, frame), last = shown[shown.length - 1];
  const done = frame >= canary.out.length, rb = canary.rolled >= 0 && frame > canary.rolled;
  const share = Plot.plot({
    ...msStyle, height: 170, width: 760, marginLeft: 55,
    x: {domain: [0, canary.out.length], label: null, axis: null}, y: {domain: [0, 100], label: "↑ % traffic to v15", grid: true},
    marks: [Plot.areaY(shown, {x: "t", y: "share", fill: ms.teal, fillOpacity: 0.35, curve: "step"}), Plot.line(shown, {x: "t", y: "share", stroke: ms.teal, strokeWidth: 2, curve: "step"})]
  });
  const err = Plot.plot({
    ...msStyle, height: 200, width: 760, marginLeft: 55,
    x: {domain: [0, canary.out.length], label: "Minutes since rollout started →"}, y: {domain: [0, 4.5], label: "↑ error rate (%)", grid: true},
    color: {domain: ["v14 champion", "v15 canary"], range: [ms.indigo, ms.rose], legend: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.line(shown, {x: "t", y: "base", stroke: () => "v14 champion", strokeWidth: 1.8}),
      Plot.line(shown.filter(d => d.v15 !== null), {x: "t", y: "v15", stroke: () => "v15 canary", strokeWidth: 1.8}),
      rb ? Plot.ruleX([canary.rolled], {stroke: ms.rose, strokeDasharray: "4,4"}) : null
    ]
  });
  const msg = rb ? `Automatic rollback at minute ${canary.rolled}: v15 errors exceeded v14 by more than ${tol} points. Only ${canary.out[canary.rolled - 1]?.share ?? 1}% of traffic was ever exposed.`
    : done ? "Rollout complete. v15 is now serving 100% of traffic; promote the 'champion' alias."
    : `Canary at ${last.share}% of traffic, metrics within tolerance.`;
  return htl.html`<div>${share}${err}<div class="ms-readout"><span>Status</span><b style="font-size:1rem">${msg}</b></div></div>`;
}
```

The point of a canary is containment. A bug that would have hit every customer touched only a small slice, for a few minutes.

## Is v15 actually better? An A/B test

Safety is not the same as improvement. To measure the business effect, PayGuard split traffic 50/50 for three weeks and counted **false declines** (good customers wrongly blocked). The simulation below tracks the difference and its 95% confidence interval as data accumulates.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ab
#| fig-cap: "Simulated A/B test. Early on, the confidence interval is wide and crosses zero; after about two weeks it sits clearly below zero, showing v15 declines fewer good customers."
#| code-fold: true
import numpy as np, plotly.graph_objects as go
from ms_charts import COLORS, PLOTLY_CONFIG
rng = np.random.default_rng(17)
days, per_day = 21, 4000
a = rng.binomial(per_day, 0.0210, days).cumsum()    # v14 false declines
b = rng.binomial(per_day, 0.0185, days).cumsum()    # v15 false declines
n = per_day * np.arange(1, days + 1)
pa, pb = a / n, b / n
diff = (pb - pa) * 100
se = np.sqrt(pa * (1 - pa) / n + pb * (1 - pb) / n) * 100
d = np.arange(1, days + 1)
fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_scatter(x=np.r_[d, d[::-1]], y=np.r_[diff + 1.96 * se, (diff - 1.96 * se)[::-1]], fill="toself",
                fillcolor="rgba(20,184,166,0.18)", line=dict(width=0), name="95% interval")
fig.add_scatter(x=d, y=diff, line=dict(color=COLORS["teal"], width=3), name="v15 minus v14")
fig.add_hline(y=0, line_color=COLORS["slate"], line_dash="dash")
fig.update_layout(height=360, xaxis_title="Day of test", yaxis_title="Difference in false-decline rate (points)", legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.12))
fig.show(config=PLOTLY_CONFIG)
```

The difference in rates and its interval are

$$
\hat\Delta = \hat p_{15} - \hat p_{14}, \qquad
\hat\Delta \pm 1.96\sqrt{\frac{\hat p_{14}(1-\hat p_{14})}{n_{14}} + \frac{\hat p_{15}(1-\hat p_{15})}{n_{15}}}
$$ {#eq-ab}

After 21 days, v15 changes the false-decline rate by **`{python} f"{diff[-1]:.2f}"` points** (95% interval `{python} f"{diff[-1]-1.96*se[-1]:.2f}"` to `{python} f"{diff[-1]+1.96*se[-1]:.2f}"`). Decide the test length **before** starting, and do not stop early the first time the interval looks good.

## Rollback must be boring

```{mermaid}
%%| echo: false
flowchart LR
  A[Metric breach<br/>or human call] --> B[Move 'champion'<br/>alias back to v14]
  B --> C[Service reloads<br/>within seconds]
  C --> D[Verify metrics<br/>recover]
  D --> E[Keep v15 for<br/>investigation]
```

Practise rollback regularly (the [Maintenance](/deployment/maintenance/ml-model-maintenance.qmd) calendar includes a quarterly drill). Keep the previous image and model available, and make sure database or schema changes are **backward compatible** so v14 can still run.

## Summary

- Version **code, data, features, model, config and environment** together.
- Use **semantic versions** and registry **aliases**; promotion and rollback become one call.
- Roll out with **shadow → canary → full**, and use an **A/B test** to prove business value.
- Automate the **rollback trigger** and practise it until it is boring.
- Back to the start: the [Deployment overview](/deployment/deployment-overview.qmd) shows how all nine parts fit together.
